S_CHG: Upstream changelogs. sysstat: the iostat fields changed in 11.5.7 (avgqu-sz became aqu-sz) and svctm was removed in 12.1.2. procps-ng: vmstat prints guest time by default since 4.0.4.
S_LPI: LPI Exam Objectives version 4.5.0, objective 200.1 'Measure and Troubleshoot Resource Usage' (exam 201-450), weight: 6. Key knowledge areas: measure CPU, memory, disk I/O and network I/O; measure firewalling and routing throughput; map client bandwidth usage; match system symptoms with likely problems; estimate throughput and identify bottlenecks. Partial list of the used files, terms and utilities: iostat, iotop, vmstat, netstat, ss, iptraf, pstree, ps, w, lsof, top, htop, uptime, sar, swap, processes blocked on I/O, blocks in, blocks out.
S_NET: Ethernet line rate: every frame occupies its size plus 20 bytes on the wire (8 bytes of preamble and 12 bytes of inter-frame gap). 64-byte frames at 1 Gb/s give 1,488,095 packets per second; at 10 Gb/s, 14,880,952 pps; 1518-byte frames at 10 Gb/s give 812,744 pps. How many packets per second a Linux router forwards per core depends on CPU, NIC, driver and ruleset, and has to be measured: there is no universal figure.
S_NODE: node_exporter, collector/vmstat_linux.go: the vmstat collector only exports the /proc/vmstat fields that match --collector.vmstat.fields, whose default is ^(oom_kill|pgpg|pswp|pg.*fault).*. So node_vmstat_pgscan_direct and node_vmstat_pgsteal_direct are not exported by default; the flag has to be widened to include pgscan and pgsteal.
S_PROV: Review finding on PR #6 of study-cybercirujas (topic lpic-2/200.1): the study material was written by a language model and no command was ever run on a host to produce its terminal output, so every sample output is illustrative and nothing was captured. The kernel string 6.8.0-45-generic is an Ubuntu kernel string, not a Debian 13 one.
S_SYS: Facts checked in debian:12 (sysstat 12.6.1) and in the Ansible docs. ansible.builtin.copy does not create the parent directories of dest. On Debian 12 sysstat-collect.service runs /usr/lib/sysstat/sa1 directly. /usr/lib/sysstat/debian-sa1 exits unless ENABLED="true" is set in /etc/default/sysstat, which ships as false.
